how-it-works.name: How it works
how-it-works.body:
# An exit plan you set yourself

Canopy watches the DeFi vaults you hold. When an alarm you chose fires, keepers try to exit your position, and the money goes back to your own wallet.

Auto-exit is live on Robinhood Chain for ERC-4626 vaults, such as Morpho's USDG vaults. The wallet check and risk cards are free.

If you hold a vault through Robinhood Earn, you can check it and follow it for alerts. Auto-exit needs a wallet you sign with yourself, so it doesn't reach positions held in the Robinhood app.

## Start with a risk card

Open the app and paste any wallet address. Your browser reads the chain directly and lists that wallet's vault positions. Nothing is signed, and the address is not sent to Canopy.

Each position gets a plain-words card of on-chain facts: who can change the vault, what it is exposed to and how much could be withdrawn right now. That last number can change quickly during a run.

## Follow a vault for free

Follow any vault in [@CanopyAlerts_Bot](https://t.me/CanopyAlerts_Bot) and get an alert when one of its alarms fires. This needs no wallet connection and no signature. The bot never signs anything; arming and exits happen in the web app.

## Choose your alarms

The app shows common presets for each vault, and you choose which to use. Nothing is armed by default.

| Alarm | When it fires |
|---|---|
| Vault loss | The share price falls 0.5% below its high |
| Pause | The vault reports that it is paused, where it has a pause switch |
| Exploit confirmed | Two of three approved watchers sign an exploit report |
| Vault drain + confirmation | Assets fall 25% within an hour, and a watcher confirms within 24 hours |
| Curator change + confirmation | The curator changes, and a watcher confirms within 24 hours |

On-chain signals like a vault loss can fire on their own. A drain or a curator change can be ordinary activity, so those need a watcher to confirm. If an alarm already fired before you arrived, the app won't let you arm it.

[Alarms](#alarms) lists every kind and the rules they all follow. An AI may label public reports for the watchers. It cannot fire an alarm, choose an amount or pick where funds go.

## Review the permission

Arming takes a few transactions, and you sign each one in your own wallet. You accept the terms, register any alarms the vault doesn't have yet, approve your vault shares to the exit contract and arm the position.

The exit contract has no "send to" field. Every exit pays the position owner, and nobody else. A rogue keeper or a false alarm can, at worst, take you out early.

Before you arm, the app reads the vault's share-transfer gates. If a gate would block the exit, it turns alarms off for that vault.

## Follow the result

When an alarm fires, keepers try the exit right away. The exit redeems your shares for the vault's own asset, such as USDG, and sends it to your wallet. There is no swap in v1. If only part of the vault is liquid, the keeper takes what it can and keeps trying while the alarm is live.

Every exit is a public transaction on Robinhood Chain, and you get a link to it.

## Revoke when you want

Exit Now and Disarm All are always free. One transaction disarms every position. You can also revoke the vault approval, and you can always withdraw from the vault directly, as usual. Getting back into a position is up to you.

alarms.name: Alarms
alarms.body:
# Seven kinds of alarm

An alarm is a public rule in the alarm contract. Anyone can register one, and anyone can check whether it has fired. When you arm a position, you choose which alarms are allowed to exit it.

## What the app offers

These are the presets the app shows for each vault. Nothing is armed by default.

| Alarm | Fires when |
|---|---|
| Vault loss | The vault's share price falls 0.5% below its recorded high |
| Pause | The vault reports that it is paused. Offered only where the vault has a pause switch |
| Exploit confirmed | 2 of the 3 approved watchers sign the same exploit report |
| Vault drain + confirmation | Assets fall 25% within an hour, and the watchers confirm within 24 hours |
| Curator change + confirmation | The vault's curator changes, and the watchers confirm within 24 hours |

A drain or a curator change can be ordinary activity, so on their own they never exit anyone. They count only when paired with a watcher confirmation.

## Every kind the contract knows

| Kind | What it reads |
|---|---|
| SHARE_DROP | The vault's share price against its high-water mark |
| PAUSED | The vault's own paused() switch |
| ADDRESS_CHANGE | A role on the vault, such as its curator |
| DRAIN | The vault's total assets over a time window |
| QUORUM | Signatures from approved watchers |
| BOTH | Two other alarms firing within a window |
| PRICE_BELOW | A price feed against a floor. Built in, not offered on launch vaults |

## Rules every alarm follows

- **It must fire after you armed.** An alarm that fired before you arrived can't exit you, and the app won't offer it.
- **A fired alarm stays live for 24 hours.** While it is live, any keeper can run the exit for positions armed with it.
- **Up to 8 alarms per position.** Arming again replaces the list.
- **Baselines only move one way.** A vault's recorded high only rises. Canopy's keeper records it about once an hour, and anyone else can too.
- **The app fits alarms to the vault.** It won't offer an alarm the vault can't support, or one that has already fired.

## Watchers

Watchers are separate services that read an allowlist of public sources, such as rekt.news, Cointelegraph's hacks feed and stablecoin and network status pages. An AI labels each new post, for example as a confirmed exploit or a rumour. A label alone does nothing. An exploit alarm fires only when 2 of the 3 approved watchers sign the same report on-chain.

The approved watcher list stays with the admin permanently, so a misbehaving watcher can always be removed. A wrong watcher alarm can't be challenged on-chain in v1. If one happens, Canopy removes the responsible watcher and publishes what happened.

## Alerts use the same alarms

When you follow a vault in [@CanopyAlerts_Bot](https://t.me/CanopyAlerts_Bot), you get a message when one of that vault's preset alarms fires, with a link to the evidence. Alerts need no wallet and no signature.

fees.name: Fees
fees.body:
# Know what you are paying for

| What | Price |
|---|---|
| Wallet check and risk cards | Free |
| Vault alerts in Telegram | Free |
| Exit Now and Disarm All | Free |
| Armed plan | $15 for 3 months, or $60 a year, per wallet |
| Per-exit fee | None. Canopy's keepers pay the gas |

The Armed plan is paid in USDG on Robinhood Chain, as one transfer from your wallet. There is no standing fee allowance. Your own transactions, such as arming, need a little ETH on Robinhood Chain for gas.

## Three different things you sign

The vault approval lets the exit contract move your vault shares, and only into an exit that pays you. Arming tells the contract which alarms can trigger that exit. The plan payment is a separate USDG transfer. Review each one in your wallet before you sign it.

## Fees never touch an exit

The exit contract has no fee logic. It doesn't check whether you paid. Canopy's own keepers run exits for paid wallets, and anyone can run an exit for any armed position using the open-source keeper. Exit Now stays free for everyone.

A fee doesn't change what an exit can do. Available liquidity, share gates and contract behavior still matter, and a false alarm can still cause an unneeded exit.

## No token

Canopy has no token, and it doesn't need one to work.

exit-limits.name: Exit limits
exit-limits.body:
# What can stop an exit

Canopy tries to exit when the alarms you chose fire. It does not promise that you get out first, and it does not cover losses.

## Liquidity can run out

A lending vault may have most of its money lent out. If nothing is idle, nobody can withdraw, and that includes Canopy. Canopy withdraws whatever is liquid and keeps trying while the alarm is live, but that doesn't create liquidity.

## Crowded exits race each other

If many people arm the same vault, they compete for the same liquidity. Being first stops being an edge when everyone is armed.

## Share gates can block an exit

A curator who turns on share-transfer gates can stop the standard exit. The launch vaults have permanently given up that power, with no gate on. A curator could also lock a gate on for good, so the app reads each vault's gates before arming, and risk cards warn when a gate is on or could be.

## Alarms can be wrong

A large honest withdrawal can look like a drain. Requiring a watcher to confirm softer signals reduces false fires, but can't remove them. An unneeded exit gives up your position and can add to a run on a rumour.

## You get the vault's own asset

There is no swap in v1. If a stablecoin itself is failing, an exit from a vault in that stablecoin doesn't help, so Canopy doesn't offer a price alarm on those vaults.

## Contracts and watchers carry risk

The exit contract is new code and hasn't had an external audit yet. It can't be upgraded, and its source is published and verified, but a bug could still cost money. Contract settings change only when 2 of 3 signers on a multisig approve, and a change takes effect when signed, with no waiting period. No setting can redirect a payout. The exit contract's settings lock 12 months after launch, while approving and removing watchers stays possible.

At launch, Canopy runs a short list of approved watchers on separate infrastructure. A wrong watcher alarm can't be challenged on-chain in v1. If one happens, Canopy removes the responsible watcher and publishes what happened.

## Keepers run paid wallets

Canopy's keepers run exits for wallets on the Armed plan. Free users have Exit Now, and anyone can run the open-source keeper for any armed position.

Third-party names identify networks and protocols Canopy works with. They do not imply endorsement or partnership.

security.name: Admin and security
security.body:
# Admin and security

The short version: no one, including Canopy, can send your funds anywhere except your own wallet. The admin can change a few settings for 12 months, and then the exit contract has no admin at all.

## What can never happen

- **A payout to anyone but you.** The exit function has no recipient field. Every transfer out of the router goes to the position owner.
- **An exit that is blocked.** No pause, fee, plan check or price check can stop an exit. If an optional step can't run, the exit still pays you the vault's own asset.
- **An upgrade.** The contracts have no proxy and no upgrade path. New features come as new adapters or new contracts you choose to use.
- **A fee taken from an exit.** The router has no fee logic.

## What the admin can do

The admin is a Timelock with no delay, controlled by a 2-of-3 Safe. Until November 4, 2027 it can:

- Allow or disallow an adapter. Disallowing one never affects positions already armed with it.
- Set a price feed and its staleness limit.
- Set a swap route for the optional stablecoin exit.
- Change the guardian.

It can't move funds, change who gets paid, disarm a position, block an exit or change an armed position's alarms. After November 4, 2027 every one of these functions stops working, permanently.

## What the guardian can do

The guardian Safe can pause **new** arming, until November 4, 2027. Exits, disarming and claims keep working while arming is paused. It exists for one case: stopping new users from arming while a problem is investigated.

## Watchers stay removable

The alarm book's watcher list stays with the admin with no end date, so a bad watcher can always be removed. Registering alarms is open to anyone, and no one can remove an alarm once registered.

## When a payout can't be delivered

If a transfer to your wallet fails, for example because a token blocks it, the amount is recorded as owed to you and you can claim it later. If your wallet can't receive ETH, it gets WETH instead.

## Why there's no admin delay

A delay protects users from a surprise admin change by giving them time to leave. Here the admin can't touch funds or payouts, and you can disarm in one transaction at any time, so the team chose to launch with no delay. Every admin change is a public transaction from the admin Safe.

## Audit status

The contracts haven't had an external audit yet. They have unit, fuzz and fork tests against the live vaults, and the source is verified with an exact match. Treat them as new code, and arm only what you're comfortable with.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.body:
# What stays in your browser

Canopy never asks for a seed phrase, a login, an email address or any ID.

## Wallet checks

When you check a wallet, your browser reads the chain through a public Robinhood Chain node. The address you paste is not sent to Canopy. Your browser fetches the risk card for every listed vault at once, so the Canopy server can't tell which vaults a wallet holds.

## Wallet connections

Connecting a wallet lets the page build transactions for you to sign. Your browser builds every transaction, and your wallet shows it to you before anything is sent. Canopy never holds your keys.

## Phone wallets

If you choose a phone wallet, the page loads WalletConnect and shows a QR code. The connection runs through WalletConnect's relay, operated by Reown, which passes messages between the page and your wallet. Reown can see that a connection happened, but not your keys. Desktop browser wallets don't use it.

## Alerts

The Telegram bot knows which vaults you follow and your Telegram chat, because it has to message you. It doesn't need your wallet.

## Website resources

Fonts, images and video are served with this website. The phone wallet screen loads its own font from Reown. This site has no analytics or tracking scripts. The hosting service may process normal web requests.

contracts.name: Contracts
contracts.body:
# Contracts and addresses

Canopy runs on Robinhood Chain (chain ID 4663). Every contract below is verified on Blockscout and Sourcify with an exact match to the [public source](https://github.com/CanopyRH/canopy-app/tree/main/contracts). None of them can be upgraded.

## Contracts

| Contract | Address | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| ExitRouter | [0xC867…965C](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0xC867A4B38f7B9F7CCc121D61b2F8d200395a965C) | Holds the arming rules and runs exits. Pays the position owner only |
| AlarmBook | [0x550c…6e4d](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x550cC2Ad4c2f095c37B8362bd19c475Ab7576e4d) | The public alarm registry. Anyone can register or check an alarm |
| ERC4626Adapter | [0x14E6…98BC](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x14E6f3a2Cd259148f983E2b01Fe778c5002c98BC) | Redeems ERC-4626 vault shares for the vault's asset |
| Timelock | [0xA371…0D9b](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0xA37196aCb22146424C1984001c18F49877B10D9b) | The admin of the router and the alarm book, run by the admin Safe |

## Safes

Each Safe is a 2-of-3 multisig.

| Safe | Address | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Admin | [0xa214…5c91](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0xa21499ea134b8752c0376062B9b5cf1b48665c91) | Proposes admin changes through the Timelock |
| Guardian | [0x3174…033A](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x31744293C35b42a3089dCbB4B171836397aA033A) | Can pause new arming only |
| Payments | [0xb668…95ad](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0xb668d6822b09eA5D32606e78Ed81d10C34CB95ad) | Receives Armed plan payments. Has no role in any contract |

## Settings fixed at deploy

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Stablecoin | USDG, [0x5fc5…d168](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168) |
| USDG price feed | [0x8bEe…1c2e](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x8bEeE3503F6860D5dac4cE26b5eEe92982951c2e), treated as stale after 25 hours |
| Timelock delay | 0. A change applies as soon as 2 of 3 admin signers approve it |
| Admin and guardian end | November 4, 2027, 00:00 UTC. After that the router has no admin |
| Alarm lifetime | 24 hours after firing |
| Alarms per position | Up to 8 |
| First block | 106087816 |

See [Admin and security](#security) for exactly what each role can and can't do.

keepers.name: Exits without Canopy
keepers.body:
# Exits without Canopy

Canopy's keepers run exits for wallets on the Armed plan. The contract doesn't know about plans, so you never depend on Canopy to get out.

## Exit Now

The position owner can call exit at any time, with or without an alarm, and it's always free. In the app, Exit Now sends that transaction from your wallet.

## Anyone can run an armed exit

While an alarm you armed is live, anyone can call exit for your position, and the funds still go to you. That means a friend, a script or a third-party keeper can get you out if Canopy's service is down.

## Run the open-source keeper

The keeper is in the [public repository](https://github.com/CanopyRH/canopy-app) under services/. It needs Postgres, a Robinhood Chain RPC and a key with a little ETH for gas, and it holds no user funds. Start it with ROLE=keeper and set KEEPER_PAID_ONLY=false so it runs every armed position, not just paid ones. The repository's README lists the settings.

## Call the contract by hand

On [the ExitRouter's Blockscout page](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0xC867A4B38f7B9F7CCc121D61b2F8d200395a965C?tab=read_write_contract), use Write contract:

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| exit(posId, alarmKey, amount) | Exits a position. The owner can pass any alarm key; anyone else needs a live alarm the owner armed |
| disarm(posId) | Disarms one position. Owner only |
| disarmAll() | Disarms every position of the caller in one transaction |
| claimOwed(owner, token) | Sends any owed amount to its owner |

Read contract has positionId(owner, adapter, target, tokenId) to find a position's ID. For vault shares, tokenId is 0 and adapter is the ERC4626Adapter address.

telegram.name: Telegram alerts
telegram.body:
# Telegram alerts

[@CanopyAlerts_Bot](https://t.me/CanopyAlerts_Bot) sends a message when an alarm fires on a vault you follow. It's free and needs no wallet.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /start | Shows what the bot does and a button to open the app |
| /vaults | Lists the vaults with risk cards |
| /watch 0x… | Follows a vault |
| /unwatch 0x… | Stops following a vault |
| /list | Shows the vaults you follow |
| /card 0x… | Shows a vault's risk card |

You can follow up to 20 vaults.

## What it knows

The bot stores your Telegram chat and the vault addresses you follow, because it has to message you. It never asks for a wallet address, and it can't sign or send anything. Arming and exits happen only in the web app, signed in your own wallet.

## If you hold through Robinhood Earn

Alerts work for any vault, including ones you hold in the Robinhood app. Auto-exit can't reach those positions, so an alert tells you to withdraw in the app.
